text:
maria-support: hey team, escalating a live issue from AcmeHealth org — their users hit an infinite redirect when we post SAMLResponse to our ACS. Started ~12:40 UTC, affects web SSO only, mobile ok. ticket #INC-10291

acme-ops: seeing it too, login just reloads the IdP login page repeatedly after redirect back to our ACS. No SAML assertion processed.

maria-support: i captured a curl trace from their IdP -> our endpoint: 

```
$ curl -v -d "SAMLResponse=<base64>" https://login.redwood.example/saml/acs
> POST /saml/acs HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 302 Found
< Location: https://idp.acmehealth.example/login?RelayState=...\n# then browser goes back to IdP and cycle repeats
```

maria-support: the 302 is coming from our ACS, not IdP. logs show `302 -> /saml/redirect?error=invalid_request` then browser redirected to IdP.

raj-se: any errors in our SAML processing logs? can you paste request-id?

maria-support: request-id: req_0a7b9f. From our logs: 
```
2026-03-12T12:40:17Z req_0a7b9f INFO saml: received SAMLResponse size=12k
2026-03-12T12:40:17Z req_0a7b9f INFO saml: validating signature using cert thumbprint abc123
2026-03-12T12:40:17Z req_0a7b9f ERROR saml: signature verification failed - no matching public key
2026-03-12T12:40:17Z req_0a7b9f INFO saml: fallback routing -> /saml/redirect?error=invalid_request
```

julian-identity: signature failed suggests IdP rotated keys but still sending assertions signed with the old key OR our metadata doesn't contain the new cert. Did they share updated metadata?

acme-ops: they did a cert rotation this morning. They sent metadata XML but noted they used `singleLogoutService` and `artifact` endpoints too. We imported the metadata via console.

maria-support: i compared the metadata we have vs what they sent. the metadata they provided contains two <KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\"> entries. One cert matches thumbprint abc123 (old) and another is new thumbprint def456. In our console view we only show abc123. looks like the second cert didn't import.

raj-se: hmm. UI import bug? any errors during import?

maria-support: console logs show `metadata import: Warning - duplicate entityID, skipping <KeyDescriptor> at line 42` — so it appears our metadata parser skipped the second KeyDescriptor when encountering an ordering case.

julian-identity: ordering shouldn't matter. we used an XML parser that normalizes, but i remember a recent change to avoid mixed content that might reject multiple KeyDescriptors if an encryptedAssertion flag was present. could be related.

srebot: incident severity: P2 (customer impact, login blocked for subset of users). Escalation to eng-identity requested.

maria-support: also noticed ACS endpoint is behind our LB that does an http->https redirect for non-https requests. AcmeHealth's IdP posts to the ACS using the metadata ACS URL that includes a trailing slash and HTTP scheme (http://login.redwood.example/saml/acs/). Their IdP does an HTTP POST (not TLS) then LB redirects to HTTPS -> that may cause IdP to treat the response as redirect and retry.

acme-ops: they said they always POST to the URL in metadata. their metadata has ACS binding=POST and Location="http://login.redwood.example/saml/acs/" (with trailing slash).

julian-identity: two problems then: (1) cert/key lookup failure because our metadata import skipped the second KeyDescriptor, causing signature verify fail; (2) IdP is POSTing to HTTP, LB 302 causes redirect loop client-side. both combine to make auth appear to loop.

raj-se: for immediate mitigation we can: 
- update our imported metadata to include the new cert manually (workaround)
- accept both thumbprints in runtime key store without re-import 
- add a temporary 308 handling on ACS to accept POST over HTTP and internally forward to validate without 302 (dangerous but quick)

julian-identity: prefer manual metadata patch + runtime key accept. 308 for POST redirect can violate IdP POST semantics and is risky.

maria-support: customer is asking for ETA. acme-ops says many users are blocked — prefer quick manual fix.

julian-identity: i'll take it. steps i'll run now: 
1) fetch their latest metadata XML (they already uploaded)
2) run our import-tool in dry-run to reproduce skipping case 
3) patch the metadata entry in the database to include both certs (base64) and reload saml-key-cache
4) request acme to change ACS Location to https:// (preferred) but not blocking for now

julian-identity: running dry-run, found parser warning: `Skipped KeyDescriptor with no explicit use attribute when multiple present` — that's the regression. I'll push a tiny parser fix and do a hotpatch then manually patch their metadata as well.

maria-support: can you also add a quick alert to the console UI so admins see "Missing cert detected" when we detect signature mismatches? customer got confused.

julian-identity: yep will add an admin alert and a console note on the org.

acme-ops: i'm preparing repro steps for legal/ops: 
1) login to idp admin, post test SAMLResponse to http://login.redwood.example/saml/acs/ 
2) observe 302 back to idp login in browser console and repeated POSTs 
3) curl -v shows 302 from LB not 200

maria-support: adding these to ticket.

raj-se: estimated timeline for hotpatch + manual metadata patch?

julian-identity: manual patch + cache reload: ~25-40m. parser hotpatch and deploy to staging: ~90m, prod rollout after smoke: +2h. I'll post status every 15m.

oncall-bot: @julian-identity assigned incident INC-10291 to eng-identity. Pager duty triggered. :bell: 

maria-support: thanks — please paste the DB patch steps here when done so i can update customer. also want a short root-cause blurb for postmortem.

julian-identity: will do. quick note for postmortem: root cause = metadata import regression skipping secondary KeyDescriptor when use attribute absent; contributing factor = IdP publishing http ACS URL (non-TLS) causing LB redirect and client-side loop. fix = import parser fix + UI warning + recommend ACS use https in metadata.

maria-support: copying to ticket and notifying AcmeHealth. :thumbsup:

srebot: update: incident severity unchanged. next status @ 1836011450.
